review_role: Independent read-only source and existing-evidence review; no product/test execution and no production/formal-test/Git changes by reviewer.

observed_failure.result: 17 of 18 CTest suites passed; direct_shared timed out at 90.03 seconds with process TIMEOUT=90.
observed_failure.interpretation: The old runner emitted PASS only after case completion and did not flush stdout. No captured case output proves neither zero progress nor a particular deadlock or slow case.

observations: Gate::wait and mock Worker fetch waits use condition_variable predicates and release their mutex during waits; release flags/sets are synchronized. The mock copies its responder/profile hook and invokes them after releasing the Worker mutex.

Running::~Running releases all Worker fetch gates, runs registered profile/window cleanup releases, then joins. New gate objects are declared before Running, so cleanup and joins precede gate/Fixture destruction.

Core cancellation marks the member under direct_reads_mutex_, unlocks, notifies subscribers and calls fetch.cancel_direct outside the coordination lock. Fixed payer waits for explicit physical mock release; tests release it before joining.

No assertion or shared mutable Json response is executed on a business thread; Outcome fields are read after join or guarded by atomic completion. This is a static review statement, not a Windows race-detector result.
synchronization_review.remaining_diagnostic_risk: Gate/Worker blocking waits and std::thread::join are unbounded. Five-second observer checks can throw, but failure unwinding can still block in Running destruction if there is an actual deadlock. Therefore those checks do not guarantee a failed test emits FAIL within five seconds. A flushed RUN line is needed to locate an unfinished case.

cost_and_capacity_review.fixture_count_basis: Static enumeration of all normal success-path loop iterations, not measured runtime events.
cost_and_capacity_review.disk_and_json_work: Fixture constructs a new on-disk Store. Store opens SQLite FULLMUTEX, sets WAL and synchronous=FULL, migrates through schema15 and commits publication setup. Tests also ingest snapshots and some open additional writers. The registry case starts 65 concurrent reads; the large-body case serializes/parses a 700 KiB control-character body and verifies a frozen snapshot over 8 MiB in each of two branches.
cost_and_capacity_review.handle_capacity_case: 1024 sequential prepare calls do a principal SELECT, RAND_bytes and bounded in-memory registry pruning/insertion; they do not each commit a persistent handle. The first 1024 prepares scan at most 0+1+...+1023 existing entries (523776 visits before later operations). Expiry is forced by the private test seam; there is no real 120-second sleep. Existing 120-second semantics remain unchanged.
cost_and_capacity_review.sixty_second_arguments: 60-second read /65-second RPC values are asserted parameters sent to a mock; they are not requested fixture sleeps. The subscriber production wait still uses its existing actual bound.

cross_environment_timing.qualification: Different OS/build/dependency/runner environments. These independent suites are roughly 5.26x to 8.03x slower and support cumulative Debug/database overhead as a plausible hypothesis. They do not measure direct_shared per-case time, establish causality, justify a performance guarantee, or prove it must finish by any chosen watchdog.

recommended_followup.change_classification: Test diagnostics plus finite Windows process watchdog only; not a demonstrated product bug fix.
recommended_followup.runner: RUN before each case; PASS/FAIL with steady_clock elapsed milliseconds; explicit flushing. Reviewed diff preserves all case/helper bytes, registration order, assertions, exception handling and failure exit status.
recommended_followup.watchdog_choice: 180 seconds would also be a bounded diagnostic run; 240 gives more observation headroom when exact Windows case costs are unknown. Neither limit guarantees completion or excludes a deadlock. Retain the original 90.03-second failure and do not repeatedly inflate the limit if one case stalls.
unchanged_requirements: 60-second direct /65-second RPC parameter contract and production subscriber waits
recommended_followup.acceptance_for_actual_new_ci: Check the exact published SHA. Require every one of the 34 RUN cases to have PASS and the original 10259-assertion/zero-failure summary, CTest success and actual Linux/Windows completion. If one RUN remains unfinished or a check fails, inspect that case/phase and thread stacks as available instead of declaring a timeout-only cause. A passing bounded suite supports that input/environment only; no full B-24/C-15 or product latency acceptance.

closed_http_review_unchanged: The original independent HTTP review/manifest remain sealed. This record concerns the newly observed baseline Windows native-suite timeout and its separate runner/watchdog follow-up.
